items.title: xscalers
items.text:
sklearn-shaped, dim-aware scaling transformers for xarray and pytensor.xtensor.

Fit is eager xarray: the fitted state is an xr.Dataset you can inspect and edit, and transform is pure arithmetic by dimension name that runs identically on DataArrays and symbolic pytensor.xtensor variables. All v1 scalers are affine, so model code binds only to a composed (center, scale) pair. Nothing custom: every container and serialization format is a native ecosystem object.

items.title: Why
items.text:
Hand-writing (x - mean) / std is fine until the regression's inputs are an xr.Dataset with mixed grains and the model is PyMC. Three familiar pains:

  • sklearn's transformers assume stacked 2-D arrays and hide fitted state in mean_-style attributes, which neither preserves dims nor hands you the fitted constants;
  • the scaling constants fed into a pytensor.xtensor graph are usually hand-copied, so converting a model contribution back to real terms goes silently wrong;
  • xarray itself ships no scaling transformer.

xscalers fills exactly that gap: affine scaling over dimension names on native xarray objects, fitted state as an inspectable xr.Dataset artifact, the same arithmetic lifting into a symbolic pytensor.xtensor graph, and one unscale verb that converts model contributions back to real units, refusing where the algebra is not affine instead of guessing.

The frame is a regression loop you can toggle: point the same pipeline at a different transformation (MeanScaler vs ZScore vs FixedScaler, per variable) and regenerate the model-ready xr.Dataset without touching model code, then invert predictions and contributions back to real terms with the same fitted state.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install xscalers            # core (xarray, numpy)
pip install "xscalers[pytensor]"  # with the symbolic pytensor extra

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
import xarray as xr

from xscalers.datasets import load_national
from xscalers.preprocessing import MeanScaler

national: xr.Dataset = load_national()

scaler = MeanScaler(("date",))
state = scaler.fit(national["media"])
scaled = scaler.transform(national["media"], state)
back = scaler.inverse_transform(scaled, state)   # round-trips exactly

items.title: The basics
items.text:
xscalers implements sklearn's transformer vocabulary, fit / transform / inverse_transform, over xarray objects:

class BaseTransformer:
    dims: tuple[str, ...] | None                       # dims to reduce over; None = all
    def fit(self, X) -> xr.Dataset                     # fitted state, inspectable + editable
    def transform(self, X, state) -> X                 # state: Mapping[str, DataArray]
    def inverse_transform(self, X, state) -> X

Dataset and DataTree inputs are handled per variable: each variable keeps its own remaining dims, which is what makes mixed-grain inputs work with no special casing.

items.title: Derived metrics
items.text:
Derive turns selected pieces of existing variables into a new variable that later steps treat like anything else. The two pieces do not have to come from the same variable or the same grain: a national series over a product-grain control broadcasts up to product grain, so tv_per_control below is a product-grain variable built from a national input.

Ops are a closed, spec-serializable vocabulary, op="ratio | diff | product", and selector pieces take reduce="sum | mean | first | last" for share-of-total style derivations.

items.title: The non-affine caveat
items.text: A log makes the target path non-affine: pipe.affine() refuses such pipelines, and real-terms contributions must go through the batched inverse_transform instead of the (beta, scale) shortcut. See Converting to real units for the honest version.

items.title: Honesty about dropped data
items.text:
Dropping destroys data, so VariableDropper.inverse_transform raises instead of guessing, and pipe.inverse_transform refuses for the whole chain. Real-terms conversion is unaffected: pipe.unscale(contrib, var="tv_per_control") still walks that one variable backwards.

fit validates rather than failing late (sklego's contract): unknown names raise KeyError, dropping every variable raises ValueError, and a non-Dataset input raises TypeError (DataTree node drops are deferred).

items.title: Selector
items.text:
If you need the reverse, a pipeline that scales what it keeps:

  • Splitter is the invertible way to split one variable into differently-treated pieces (see Splitting);
  • VariableTransformer(..., remainder="drop") is the leftover-dropping sibling.

items.title: VariableTransformer
items.text:
VariableTransformer is the ColumnTransformer analog over named data variables instead of column positions:

  • explicit mapping of variable name to transformer;
  • remainder="passthrough" leaves unknown variables untouched;
  • remainder="drop" removes them, the leftover-dropping sibling of the standalone drop verb (Dropping).

items.title: State per variable
items.text:
Because each variable is fitted independently, the state is a mapping of variable name to its own xr.Dataset. That is what lets a national series and a per-product series live side by side with separate fitted constants, and what Pipeline.affine() composes into one (center, scale) pair per variable downstream.

items.title: Saving the fitted state
items.text: State is data: saving it is native xarray IO, in any of the three shapes you'll meet in practice.

items.title: 1. A standalone one-file artifact
items.text:
to_netcdf, next to your recipe:

import os

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from xscalers.datasets import load_national
from xscalers.preprocessing import MeanScaler

national: xr.Dataset = load_national()
scaler = MeanScaler(dims=("date",))
state = scaler.fit(national["media"])

state.to_netcdf("media_state.nc")                 # state is a Dataset — native IO
reloaded = xr.open_dataset("media_state.nc")      # ...read back natively
scaled = scaler.transform(national["media"], reloaded)
back = scaler.inverse_transform(scaled, reloaded)
np.testing.assert_allclose(back, national["media"])
print("media_state.nc round-trips exactly")
os.remove("media_state.nc")                       # tidy up after this example
media_state.nc round-trips exactly

items.title: 2. Alongside your (large) zarr inputs
items.text:
Append the state tree as groups of the existing store. append_state exists only because DataTree.to_zarr(group=...) is not implemented upstream; reading back is native.

from pathlib import Path

import xarray as xr

from xscalers.compose import VariableTransformer
from xscalers.container import state_tree
from xscalers.datasets import load_mixed_grain
from xscalers.persistence import append_state

store: Path = Path("inputs.zarr")                 # your existing input store
mixed: xr.Dataset = load_mixed_grain()            # pretend it already lives there
mixed.to_zarr(store)                              # ... here we create it first

transformer: VariableTransformer = VariableTransformer(
    {"media_national": MeanScaler(dims=("date",))},
    remainder="drop",
)
state = transformer.fit(mixed)
append_state(state_tree({"scale": state}), store, group="scalers")

reloaded_tree = xr.open_datatree(store, group="scalers")
reloaded_state = {
    name: node.dataset for name, node in reloaded_tree.children["scale"].children.items()
}
scaled_again = transformer.transform(mixed, reloaded_state)
print(f"reloaded state vars: {sorted(reloaded_state)}")
import shutil; shutil.rmtree(store)               # tidy up after this example
reloaded state vars: ['media_national']

mode="a" means a refit overwrites the group: name groups per fit if you want history.

items.title: 3. Next to a PyMC model
items.text:
The state and the InferenceData are separate artifacts sharing a directory; the recipe (JSON via to_spec) is versioned config, state is data, never the two mixed.

# requires-pymc
import pymc as pm

from xscalers.datasets import load_national
from xscalers.preprocessing import MeanScaler

national = load_national()
scaler = MeanScaler(dims=("date",))
state = scaler.fit(national["target"])
y = scaler.transform(national["target"], state)   # scaled input into the model

with pm.Model() as model:
    beta = pm.Normal("beta", 0, 1)
    sigma = pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1)
    # numpy views into the scaled dataset operate the same as scaled arrays
    pm.Normal("obs", beta * float(y.mean()), sigma, observed=np.asarray(y))
    idata = pm.sample_prior_predictive(draws=10, random_seed=0)

Requires pymc

The whole fitted pipeline serializes as recipe + artifact, one file:

# continues above — `state` carries over
from xscalers.container import state_tree

state_tree({"scale": state}).to_netcdf("fitted_state.nc")   # one artifact

items.title: For sklearn users
items.text:
The vocabulary is deliberately sklearn-shaped:

sklearn xscalers notes fit / transform / inverse_transform same states are xr.Datasets, not attributes ColumnTransformer VariableTransformer per-variable treatment over named data variables ColumnDropper (sklego) VariableDropper over drop_vars / drop_sel Pipeline Pipeline named steps, chained states, reversed inverse make_pipeline make_pipeline the composition verb FeatureUnion make_union many pipelines over one dataset, collision policy, covariates-only by design "passthrough" "passthrough" identical semantics

items.title: The deliberate departure
items.text: State is explicit and passed around, not hidden as scaler.mean_. That is what lets you edit fitted values, reuse them across backends, and serialize them with native xarray IO. It is also why transform takes the state as an argument instead of reading private attributes.

items.title: The counterpart to transform
items.text: For model code the companion verb is unscale: one call, correct for affine pipelines and honest for non-affine ones (it refuses where the algebra does not hold instead of returning a wrong pair).

items.title: What is not here, on purpose
items.text:
• >> / | operator chaining: make_pipeline / make_union are the way to compose (Kedro-style chaining reads like imperative execution and hides the recipe/state split).
  • Aggregation and dedup: stay upstream xarray ops (resample, groupby, drop_duplicates), outside the pipeline.

items.title: Splitting one variable into differently-treated pieces
Why pieces are siblings
items.text: A Dataset cannot hold two variables with disjoint values on the same dim (merge outer-joins), so each piece's split dim is renamed {dim}_{piece}, and inverse_transform renames back and restores the original coordinates. On DataTree inputs, pieces become child nodes under the source node instead, keeping the same invertibility.

items.title: Splits are affine identities
items.text: The split is a value-preserving selection, so the composed affine answer composes through it: pipe.affine() gives each created piece its own (center, scale) pair, with the source variable (gone post-step) getting no pair.

items.title: Auto-naming
items.text: make_pipeline names steps from transformer classes (zscore, zscore-1, ...), mirroring sklearn. "passthrough" is a valid step value: it fits to an empty state and transforms identity.

items.title: Reusing a fitted step elsewhere
items.text: Because a BoundStep carries its state, it serializes and moves the same way any state does (Saving the fitted state): the step's fitted behavior is data, not a hidden attribute on an object.

items.title: Converting to real units: unscale
items.text: Model code never hand-writes x * scale + center: the affine pair is an internal detail. Pipeline.unscale applies the composed pair per variable (eager xarray contributions or symbolic pytensor.xtensor in the graph). When a pipeline is non-affine (e.g. a log-derived metric), unscale walks only that variable's own steps backwards, stopping at the step that created it, so the one call stays honest where hand-written beta * scale algebra goes silently wrong.

items.title: Symbolic: unscale inside the pymc graph
items.text:
Requires the optional pytensor extra (pip install "xscalers[pytensor]").

# requires-pytensor
import pytensor.xtensor as ptx

from xscalers.compose import VariableTransformer
from xscalers.datasets import load_national
from xscalers.pipeline import Pipeline
from xscalers.preprocessing import MeanScaler

scaler = MeanScaler(dims=("date",))
data = load_national()
pipe = Pipeline([("scale", VariableTransformer({"media": scaler}))])
state = pipe.fit(data)                                     # fitted pipeline state

contrib = ptx.xtensor("channel_contrib", dims=("date", "channel"))
spend_real = pipe.unscale(contrib, var="media", state=state)   # symbolic: contrib * mean
print(f"symbolic result: {type(spend_real).__name__}")
symbolic result: XTensorVariable

items.title: binding
items.text:
Lift fitted xarray states into pytensor.xtensor graphs — and transform symbolically.

The flagship flow: fit is eager xarray (stats are data); transform / inverse_transform are elementwise arithmetic that work identically on DataArrays and XTensorVariables. lift_state bridges the two — via ptx.as_xtensor, which takes DataArrays natively (dims preserved, coords stripped) and is idempotent for entries that are already symbolic, which is what makes prior-over-scale ("learnable") states supported for free.

items.title: lift_state(state)
items.text:
Coerce every state entry into an XTensorVariable/constant.

Source code in src/xscalers/binding.py 
def lift_state(state: Mapping) -> dict:
    """Coerce every state entry into an XTensorVariable/constant."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in state.items():
        if is_symbolic(value):
            out[key] = value
        elif isinstance(value, xr.DataArray):
            out[key] = _as_symbol(value)
        elif isinstance(value, xr.Dataset):
            for entry, da in value.data_vars.items():
                out[str(entry)] = _as_symbol(da)
        else:
            import pytensor.xtensor as ptx

            out[key] = ptx.as_xtensor(np.asarray(value.item() if hasattr(value, "item") else value))
    return out

Lift only when the input is symbolic; xarray passes through untouched.

def lift_state_if_symbolic(X: Any, state: Mapping) -> Mapping:
    """Lift only when the input is symbolic; xarray passes through untouched."""
    if not is_symbolic(X):
        return state
    return lift_state(state)

items.title: compose
items.text:
VariableTransformer — the ColumnTransformer analog, one unit per variable.

Mirroring sklearn.compose: a map from variable (or DataTree node) to transformer, applied per unit. Mixed-grain inputs need no special casing — each variable's fitted state keeps that variable's own remaining dims. Unmapped variables pass through or drop, mirroring ColumnTransformer(remainder="passthrough") / remainder="drop".

Fitted state for this composite is dict[str, xr.Dataset] (one Dataset per variable), which state_tree nests into the canonical DataTree artifact.

items.title: VariableTransformer
items.text:
Map variables/data-tree nodes onto their own transformers.

remainder is either "passthrough" (unknown keys are left untouched, the sklearn remainder semantics) or another transformer applied to every variable without an explicit entry. default is a deprecated alias kept so older specs and call sites load unchanged.

Source code in src/xscalers/compose.py 
@register
class VariableTransformer:
    """Map variables/data-tree nodes onto their own transformers.

    ``remainder`` is either ``"passthrough"`` (unknown keys are left untouched,
    the sklearn ``remainder`` semantics) or another transformer applied to
    every variable without an explicit entry. ``default`` is a deprecated
    alias kept so older specs and call sites load unchanged.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, mapping: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, remainder: Any = "passthrough", default: Any = None
    ):
        """Build the dispatch table from the mapping and remainder policy."""
        self.mapping = dict(mapping or {})
        self.remainder = default if default is not None else remainder

    # -- key matching ------------------------------------------------------

    def _scaler_for(self, key: str) -> Any:
        if key in self.mapping:
            return self.mapping[key]
        for mapped, scaler in self.mapping.items():
            if key.endswith(f"/{mapped}"):
                return scaler
        return self.remainder

    @staticmethod
    def _apply(scaler: Any, op: str, da: Any, state: Any) -> Any:
        method = getattr(scaler, op)
        if op == "transform" or op == "inverse_transform":
            return method(da, state)
        return method(da)

    # -- transformer API ---------------------------------------------------

    def fit(self, X: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Fit each mapped variable with its own scaler.

        Returns a mapping from variable key to that scaler's stamped state.
        Unmapped variables get the remainder policy and produce no state.
        """
        items = flatten(X)
        self._warn_on_missing_keys(items)
        states: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, da in items.items():
            scaler = self._scaler_for(key)
            if scaler == "passthrough" or scaler == "drop":
                continue
            # stamped with the *scaler's* recipe: the leaf states are the
            # provenance units, not the dispatch wrapper around them
            states[key] = _stamp_state(scaler.compute(da), scaler)
        return states

    def _warn_on_missing_keys(self, items: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Explicit mapping entries naming absent variables are config bugs.

        Coordinates (e.g. `date`) are never dispatch keys — a recipe naming
        one would otherwise pass through silently under passthrough defaults.
        Suffix matches (split pieces like 'media/digital' ↔ 'digital') are
        legitimate, so they don't warn.
        """
        item_keys = list(items)

        def _matched(key: str) -> bool:
            return any(k == key or k.endswith(f"/{key}") for k in item_keys)

        missing = [k for k in self.mapping if not _matched(k)]
        if not missing:
            return
        for key in missing:
            import difflib

            suggestion = difflib.get_close_matches(key, item_keys, n=1)
            hint = f"; did you mean {suggestion[0]!r}?" if suggestion else ""
            import warnings

            warnings.warn(
                f"VariableTransformer mapping key {key!r} is missing from the input's "
                f"data variables{hint} (coordinates or DataTree children "
                "cannot be scaled directly); the variable will pass through unscaled.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=3,
            )

    def transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Scale each mapped variable with its fitted state.

        Unknown or passthrough variables pass through unchanged.
        """
        out: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, da in flatten(X).items():
            scaler = self._scaler_for(key)
            if scaler == "drop":
                continue
            st = state.get(key)
            if st is None:
                out[key] = da
            else:
                out[key] = scaler.transform(da, st)
        return reassemble(X, out)

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Unscale each mapped variable back to its original units.

        Dropped variables are not restored, mirroring ``transform``.
        """
        out: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, da in flatten(X).items():
            scaler = self._scaler_for(key)
            st = state.get(key)
            if st is None or scaler == "drop":
                out[key] = da
            else:
                out[key] = scaler.inverse_transform(da, st)
        return reassemble(X, out)

    @classmethod
    def describe(cls, spec):
        """One row per mapped variable: the leaf class describes itself."""
        from .core import REGISTRY
        from .serialize import _recipe_line

        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for variable, leaf in spec["mapping"].items():
            if not isinstance(leaf, Mapping) or "kind" not in leaf:
                continue  # passthrough strings leave no rows
            leaf_cls = REGISTRY.get(leaf["kind"])
            if leaf_cls is not None:
                rows.extend({**r, "variable": variable} for r in leaf_cls.describe(leaf["kwargs"]))
            else:
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "variable": variable,
                        "role": "transformed",
                        "kind": leaf["kind"],
                        "recipe": _recipe_line(leaf),
                        "op": "",
                        "affine": False,
                    }
                )
        return rows

    def affine_view(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Per-variable affine views from this step's states.

        Raises TypeError naming the transformer for non-affine recipes —
        the contract ``Pipeline.affine`` documents.
        """
        views: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, ds in state.items():
            scaler = self._scaler_for(key)
            view = getattr(scaler, "affine_view", None)
            if view is None:
                raise TypeError(
                    f"Variable {key!r} is mapped to a non-affine transformer "
                    f"({type(scaler).__name__}); the pipeline has no composed "
                    "(center, scale) pair for it. Use Pipeline.unscale."
                )
            views[key] = view(ds)
        return views

    def to_spec_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize the mapping and remainder into plain-dict spec kwargs."""
        from .core import to_spec

        # "passthrough" (and any other bare string) is a documented value, not
        # a transformer -- leave it alone instead of trying to spec it
        mapping = {
            key: to_spec(scaler) if not isinstance(scaler, str) else scaler
            for key, scaler in self.mapping.items()
        }
        remainder = self.remainder
        if not isinstance(remainder, str):
            remainder = to_spec(remainder)
        return {"mapping": mapping, "remainder": remainder}

    """One row per mapped variable: the leaf class describes itself."""
    from .core import REGISTRY
    from .serialize import _recipe_line

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for variable, leaf in spec["mapping"].items():
        if not isinstance(leaf, Mapping) or "kind" not in leaf:
            continue  # passthrough strings leave no rows
        leaf_cls = REGISTRY.get(leaf["kind"])
        if leaf_cls is not None:
            rows.extend({**r, "variable": variable} for r in leaf_cls.describe(leaf["kwargs"]))
        else:
            rows.append(
                {
                    "variable": variable,
                    "role": "transformed",
                    "kind": leaf["kind"],
                    "recipe": _recipe_line(leaf),
                    "op": "",
                    "affine": False,
                }
            )
    return rows

def fit(self, X: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fit each mapped variable with its own scaler.

    Returns a mapping from variable key to that scaler's stamped state.
    Unmapped variables get the remainder policy and produce no state.
    """
    items = flatten(X)
    self._warn_on_missing_keys(items)
    states: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, da in items.items():
        scaler = self._scaler_for(key)
        if scaler == "passthrough" or scaler == "drop":
            continue
        # stamped with the *scaler's* recipe: the leaf states are the
        # provenance units, not the dispatch wrapper around them
        states[key] = _stamp_state(scaler.compute(da), scaler)
    return states

    Dropped variables are not restored, mirroring ``transform``.

def flatten(X: Any) -> dict[str, xr.DataArray]:
    """Flatten any accepted container into ``key → DataArray``."""
    if isinstance(X, xr.DataArray):
        return {str(X.name) if X.name is not None else "__array__": X}
    if isinstance(X, xr.Dataset):
        return {str(var): da for var, da in X.data_vars.items()}
    if isinstance(X, xr.DataTree):
        out: dict[str, xr.DataArray] = {}
        for node in X.subtree:
            data_vars = [(str(var), da) for var, da in node.dataset.data_vars.items()]
            if not data_vars:
                continue
            parts = _node_path_parts(node)
            multi = len(data_vars) > 1
            for var, da in data_vars:
                if multi:
                    out["/".join([*parts, var]) if parts else var] = da
                elif parts:
                    out["/".join(parts)] = da
                else:
                    out[var] = da
        return out
    raise TypeError(f"Cannot flatten {type(X).__name__}")

def reassemble(X: Any, out: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray]) -> Any:
    """Rebuild the input container type from transformed flat items."""
    if isinstance(X, xr.DataArray):
        (only,) = out.values()
        return only
    if isinstance(X, xr.Dataset):
        # flat keys are exactly var names; new keys (e.g. splitter pieces)
        # appear alongside kept ones, dropped keys are absent from `out`
        return xr.Dataset(dict(out))
    if isinstance(X, xr.DataTree):
        groups = _groups_from_keys(X, out)
        root = xr.Dataset()
        tree_kwargs = {f"/{path}": xr.Dataset(vars_) for path, vars_ in groups.items()}
        return xr.DataTree.from_dict({"": root, **tree_kwargs})
    raise TypeError(f"Cannot reassemble {type(X).__name__}")

def state_from_tree(tree: xr.DataTree) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Invert ``state_tree``: a DataTree → nested mapping with Dataset leaves."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for node in tree.subtree:
        # attr-only Datasets count too (e.g. shape-step states) — only
        # fully-empty root/intermediates are skipped
        meaningful = bool(list(node.dataset.data_vars)) or bool(node.dataset.attrs)
        if not meaningful or node.path == "/":
            continue
        parts = [p for p in node.path.split("/") if p]
        branch = out
        for part in parts[:-1]:
            branch = branch.setdefault(part, {})
        branch[parts[-1]] = node.dataset
    return out

def state_tree(states: Mapping[str, Any]) -> xr.DataTree:
    """Nest fitted states into a DataTree: child per step, leaf per variable.

    ``states`` is a mapping step name → Dataset, or → another mapping
    (composite states recurse, e.g. a Union's per-branch pipeline states).
    This is what makes whole-pipeline state a single netCDF artifact.
    """
    groups: dict[str, xr.Dataset] = {}

    def _walk(prefix: str, mapping: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        for name, value in mapping.items():
            path = "/".join(filter(None, (prefix, name)))
            if isinstance(value, xr.Dataset):
                groups[path] = value
            elif isinstance(value, Mapping):
                _walk(path, value)
            else:
                raise TypeError(f"Cannot place state at {path!r}: {type(value).__name__}")

    _walk("", states)
    root = xr.Dataset()
    paths = {f"/{k}": v for k, v in groups.items()}
    return xr.DataTree.from_dict({"": root, **paths})

class BaseAffineTransformer(BaseTransformer):
    """Scalers whose transform is the affine pair: y = (x - center) / scale.

    States carry *statistics* — the entries people think in (``mean``,
    ``std``); ``PAIR`` maps the affine *roles* onto those entries. A role
    with no entry (divisive scalers have no center) defaults to ``0.0``.
    The composed affine *view* (``affine_view``) always carries both
    roles, so downstream contracts (``affine()``, ``unscale()``) stay total.
    """

    PAIR: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {"center": "center", "scale": "scale"}

    @classmethod
    def _entry(cls, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset, role: str) -> Any:
        entry = cls.PAIR.get(role)
        if entry is None or entry not in state:
            if role == "scale":
                raise KeyError(f"no {entry!r} entry for the scale role in {sorted(map(str, state))}")
            return xr.DataArray(0.0)  # center: additive identity
        return state[entry]

    def _transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        from .binding import lift_state_if_symbolic

        state = lift_state_if_symbolic(X, state)
        return (X - self._entry(state, "center")) / self._entry(state, "scale")

    def _inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        from .binding import lift_state_if_symbolic

        state = lift_state_if_symbolic(X, state)
        return X * self._entry(state, "scale") + self._entry(state, "center")

    def affine_view(self, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The composed affine roles for this scaler's state — always total."""
        return {"center": self._entry(state, "center"), "scale": self._entry(state, "scale")}

class BaseTransformer(ABC):
    """The xscalers contract, sklearn vocabulary over ecosystem-native objects."""

    @classmethod
    def describe(cls, spec: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Provenance rows this kind contributes to the ``provenance`` walk.

        Spec kwargs in, plain dicts out. Default: one transformed row
        with no known variable; step-shaped transformers (splitters, derivers,
        droppers, function maps) override to declare their variables, roles,
        and ops, so customs are first-class without library edits.
        """
        from .serialize import _recipe_line

        return [
            {
                "variable": None,
                "role": "transformed",
                "kind": cls.__name__,
                "recipe": _recipe_line({"kind": cls.__name__, "kwargs": dict(spec)}),
                "op": "",
                "affine": hasattr(cls, "affine_view"),
            }
        ]

    dims: tuple[str, ...] | None

    def __init__(self, dims: tuple[str, ...] | str | None = None):
        """Store the reduce-over dims; a bare string becomes a 1-tuple."""
        self.dims = (dims,) if isinstance(dims, str) else dims

    @abstractmethod
    def compute(self, X: Any) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Data-derived fitted state."""

    def _transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def fit(self, X: Any) -> Any:
        """Fit: DataArrays (and symbolic inputs) directly; containers via dispatch.

        Stamps ``spec_sha`` provenance onto the returned state leaves
        (best-effort; see ``_stamp_state``).
        """
        from .compose import VariableTransformer

        if self.__scalarish(X):
            return _stamp_state(self.compute(X), self)
        return _stamp_state(VariableTransformer(remainder=self).fit(X), self)

    def transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Apply the fitted arithmetic to ``X``.

        Direct for scalarish inputs, dispatched per variable for containers.
        """
        from .compose import VariableTransformer

        if self.__scalarish(X):
            return self._transform(X, state)
        return VariableTransformer(remainder=self).transform(X, state)

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Invert the transform on ``X``.

        Direct for scalarish inputs, dispatched per variable for containers.
        """
        from .compose import VariableTransformer

        if self.__scalarish(X):
            return self._inverse_transform(X, state)
        return VariableTransformer(remainder=self).inverse_transform(X, state)

    @staticmethod
    def __scalarish(X: Any) -> bool:
        """True for non-Dataset inputs, which compute/transform handle directly."""
        return not isinstance(X, xr.Dataset)

    def to_spec(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize this transformer into a plain-dict recipe spec."""
        from .serialize import spec_of

        return spec_of(self)

    def _reduce_dims(self, X: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Dims of X to reduce over: ``None`` means all of them."""
        data_dims: tuple[str, ...] | None = (
            tuple(str(d) for d in X.dims) if isinstance(X, xr.DataArray) else None
        )
        if self.dims is None:
            return _all_dims(X, data_dims)
        if data_dims is None:
            return tuple(self.dims)
        return tuple(d for d in self.dims if d in data_dims)

def as_state(
    kind: str,
    dims: tuple[str, ...] | None,
    scaled_from: str | None = None,
    attrs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    **entries: Any,

    state = xr.Dataset({k: expand(v) for k, v in entries.items()})
    state.attrs.update(
        {
            "kind": kind,
            # None-dims (reduce over everything) persists as "__all__" for

            "dims": list(dims) if dims is not None else "__all__",

            "scaled_from": scaled_from or "",
        }
    )
    if attrs:

    return state

def spec_sha(transformer: Any) -> str:
    """Deterministic 12-hex fingerprint of a transformer's recipe.

    Source of the hash: ``to_spec`` (JSON, sort_keys). Non-serializable
    transformers raise whatever ``to_spec_kwargs`` raises — stamping is
    best-effort and callers should tolerate that.
    """
    import hashlib
    import json

Each variable is on its own dim name:

  • media_national (date, channel) — one series per channel, shared by every product. Lifting it to product grain is an upstream xarray op (see load_mixed_grain); the point is that a scaled shared series and a scaled per-product series keep separate fitted states and separate affine pairs.

  • flag (date, product) / peer_flag (date, product) — 0/1 indicators, and share (date, product) — a 0..1 proportion. Deliberately different in character from level, which is what per-variable recipes are for.

def load_panel() -> xr.Dataset:
    """Load a ``(date, product)`` panel whose inputs sit at two grains.

    Each variable is on its own dim name:

    - ``media_national (date, channel)`` — one series per channel, shared by
      every product. Lifting it to product grain is an upstream xarray op (see
      [`load_mixed_grain`][xscalers.datasets.load_mixed_grain]); the point
      is that a *scaled* shared series
      and a *scaled* per-product series keep separate fitted states and
      separate affine pairs.
    - ``media_digital (date, product, digital)`` — per-product, splittable on
      a *different* dim name, because a Dataset holds one coordinate per dim.
    - ``level (date, product)`` / ``peer_level (date, product)`` — magnitudes;
      the pair a cross-variable index is derived from.
    - ``flag (date, product)`` / ``peer_flag (date, product)`` — 0/1
      indicators, and ``share (date, product)`` — a 0..1 proportion.
      Deliberately different in character from ``level``, which is what
      per-variable recipes are for.
    - ``target (date, product)`` — the quantity to model, at product grain.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(97)
    n = 90
    n_products = 4
    level = 10 + rng.gamma(4.0, 3.0, (n, n_products))
    peer_level = 11 + rng.gamma(4.0, 3.0, (n, n_products))
    flag = (rng.random((n, n_products)) < 0.25).astype(float)
    peer_flag = (rng.random((n, n_products)) < 0.2).astype(float)
    share = rng.uniform(0.4, 1.0, (n, n_products))
    return xr.Dataset(
        {
            "media_national": (("date", "channel"), np.abs(rng.gamma(2.0, 400.0, (n, 2)))),
            "media_digital": (
                ("date", "product", "digital"),
                np.abs(rng.gamma(2.0, 30.0, (n, n_products, 2))),
            ),
            "level": (("date", "product"), level),
            "flag": (("date", "product"), flag),
            "share": (("date", "product"), share),
            "peer_level": (("date", "product"), peer_level),
            "peer_flag": (("date", "product"), peer_flag),
            "target": (
                ("date", "product"),
                50 + 6 * flag + 3 * share + 20 * flag * peer_flag + rng.normal(0, 3, (n, n_products)),
            ),
        },
        coords={
            "date": _dates(n),
            "channel": ["tv", "ooh"],
            "digital": ["search", "social"],
            "product": [f"p{i}" for i in range(1, n_products + 1)],
        },
    )

items.title: persistence
items.text:
State persistence — xarray-native, except where zarr needs a workaround.

The general picture: state is data, so it saves with plain xarray IO — state.to_netcdf(path) / xr.open_datatree(path) for a standalone artifact, and for pymc workflows the state rides in the same directory as the InferenceData (az.to_netcdf(idata, "posterior.nc")). The recipe is versioned config (to_spec, a plain JSON-ish dict); state is data — never mix the two.

The one case that is not a one-liner today is appending state into an existing (large) zarr store: DataTree.to_zarr(group=...) is not implemented upstream. append_state works around it by writing each node's Dataset with Dataset.to_zarr(..., group=..., mode="a"); reading back is native: xr.open_datatree(store, group="scalers").

A bare Dataset is written directly under group; a DataTree nests one child per step (scalers/scale/<variable>). mode="a" means a refit overwrites the group (override, not duplicate) — name groups per fit (scalers/2024-02) if you want history instead.

def append_state(
    state: xr.Dataset | xr.DataTree,
    store: str | Path,
    group: str = "scalers",
) -> str | Path:
    """Append a fitted state into an existing zarr store under ``group``.

    A bare Dataset is written directly under ``group``; a DataTree nests one
    child per step (``scalers/scale/<variable>``). ``mode="a"`` means a
    refit overwrites the group (override, not duplicate) — name groups per
    fit (``scalers/2024-02``) if you want history instead.
    """
    if isinstance(state, xr.Dataset):
        state.to_zarr(store, group=group, mode="a")
        return store
    for node in state.subtree:
        data_vars = list(node.dataset.data_vars)
        if not data_vars:
            continue  # empty intermediate nodes materialize from nested groups
        node_group = "/".join(filter(None, (group, node.path.strip("/"))))
        node.dataset.to_zarr(store, group=node_group, mode="a")
    return store

items.title: pipeline
items.text:
sklearn-shaped pipelines: named steps, chained states, reversed inverse, affine view.

Pipeline.fit collects each step's state as it transforms its way down; inverse_transform runs the chain backwards against the same states. affine composes each step's affine pair per variable — the contract downstream graph builders consume — and refuses pipelines that include non-affine steps rather than silently returning a wrong pair. The whole fitted state is one netCDF artifact via state_tree.

Ergonomics: pipe["name"] yields a bound step (transformer + its fitted state slice) that can transform new data on its own; "passthrough" is a valid step value; make_pipeline derives names from transformer classes. The whole fitted state is one netCDF artifact via state_tree.

class BoundStep:
    """A fitted step: transformer bound to its slice of the pipeline state.

    Returned by ``Pipeline.__getitem__`` — the "access transformations after
    the fact" surface. ``step.transform(X)`` uses the fitted state directly,
    so a single fitted step can be applied to fresh data or reused elsewhere.
    """

    __slots__ = ("name", "state", "transformer")

    def __init__(self, name: str, transformer: Any, state: Any):
        """Bind ``transformer`` to the fitted ``state`` under ``name``."""
        self.name = name
        self.transformer = transformer
        self.state = state

    def transform(self, X: Any) -> Any:
        """Apply the bound step's transform to ``X`` using its fitted state."""
        return self.transformer.transform(X, self.state)

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any) -> Any:
        """Invert the bound step's transform on ``X`` using its fitted state."""
        return self.transformer.inverse_transform(X, self.state)

items.title: Pipeline
items.text:
Named steps chained with their own fitted states, reversed for inverse.

Each step keeps its state under its name; affine() composes the (center, scale) pair across steps, and unscale converts scaled contributions back to real units honestly (walking only the steps that produced a variable).

Source code in src/xscalers/pipeline.py 
class Pipeline:
    """Named steps chained with their own fitted states, reversed for inverse.

    Each step keeps its state under its name; ``affine()`` composes the
    ``(center, scale)`` pair across steps, and ``unscale`` converts scaled
    contributions back to real units honestly (walking only the steps that
    produced a variable).
    """

    def __init__(self, steps: list[tuple[str, Any]]):
        """Take named ``(name, step)`` pairs; ``"passthrough"`` becomes identity."""
        self.steps = [(name, _Passthrough() if step == "passthrough" else step) for name, step in steps]
        self.states_: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    def named_steps(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Steps as a name-keyed dict, sklearn-style."""
        return dict(self.steps)

    def fit(self, X: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Fit every step in order and store the state dict in ``states_``."""
        states: dict[str, Any] = {}
        current = X
        for name, step in self.steps:
            states[name] = step.fit(current)
            current = step.transform(current, states[name])
        self.states_ = states
        return states

    def transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Apply each step in order, threading the data through the chain."""
        current = X
        for name, step in self.steps:
            current = step.transform(current, state[name])
        return current

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Apply each step's inverse in reverse order."""
        current = X
        for name, step in reversed(self.steps):
            current = step.inverse_transform(current, state[name])
        return current

    def fit_transform(self, X: Any) -> Any:
        """Fit on ``X`` and return the transformed data."""
        state = self.fit(X)
        return self.transform(X, state)

    # -- post-fit step access ------------------------------------------------

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> BoundStep:
        """Access one fitted step: ``pipe["name"]`` as a BoundStep."""
        if self.states_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Pipeline is not fitted; call fit() before step access")
        steps = self.named_steps()
        if key not in steps:
            raise KeyError(f"No step named {key!r}. Steps: {sorted(steps)}")
        return BoundStep(key, steps[key], self.states_[key])

    # -- affine composition -------------------------------------------------

    def affine(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, xr.Dataset]:
        """Composed (center, scale) per variable across all steps.

        Raises TypeError if any step is not affine — a shape-changing step
        would silently produce a wrong mapping otherwise.

        This is a *diagnostic* view of what the pipeline decided (and the
        internals behind ``unscale``); model code should call
        ``pipe.unscale(x, var=...)`` rather than applying the pair by hand.
        """
        composed: dict[str, xr.Dataset] = {}
        for (name, step), step_state in zip(self.steps, state.values(), strict=True):
            view = getattr(step, "affine_view", None)
            if view is None:
                raise TypeError(f"Step {name!r} ({type(step).__name__}) is not affine")
            for key, pair in view(step_state).items():
                center, scale = pair["center"], pair["scale"]
                if key in composed:
                    prev = composed[key]
                    # y2 = (y1 - c2) / s2 where y1 = (x - c1) / s1
                    composed[key] = xr.Dataset(
                        {"center": prev["center"] + prev["scale"] * center, "scale": prev["scale"] * scale}
                    )
                else:
                    composed[key] = xr.Dataset({"center": center, "scale": scale})
        return composed

    def unscale(self, x: Any, *, var: str, state: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Any:
        """Convert a scaled-space contribution back into real units — one verb.

        For affine pipelines this applies the composed ``(center, scale)``
        pair per variable (symbolic ``pytensor.xtensor`` contributions com-
        pose identically). For pipelines that contain non-affine steps (e.g.
        a log transform on this variable) the fallback walks *this varia-
        ble's own* steps backwards — un-log, un-scale — stopping at the step
        that *created* the variable (e.g. ``Derive``), so the result is the
        pre-pipeline value of that variable in real units, not a knock-on
        restoration of unrelated inputs. `var` names a **data variable** of
        the contributions (never a coordinate). The state defaults to the
        fitted ``states_``; pass ``state=`` explicitly for pipelines rebuilt
        from specs.
        """
        chosen = state if state is not None else self.states_
        if chosen is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Pipeline has no fitted state (was this pipeline rebuilt with "
                "from_spec?); pass state=<state> explicitly or bind one"
            )
        if any(getattr(step, "affine_view", None) is None for _, step in self.steps):
            # non-affine pipeline: partial inverse — from the last step back,
            # owned variables are inverted; creation steps STOP the walk
            current_value: Any = xr.Dataset({var: x}) if isinstance(x, xr.DataArray) else x
            if var not in current_value.data_vars:
                raise KeyError(
                    f"No data variable named {var!r}; variables: {sorted(map(str, current_value.data_vars))}"
                )
            for name, step in reversed(self.steps):
                step_state = chosen[name]
                if _step_creates_var(step, step_state, var):
                    break  # stop *before* the step that created the variable
                if _step_owns(step, step_state, var):
                    current_value = step.inverse_transform(current_value, step_state)
            if isinstance(x, xr.DataArray):
                return current_value[var]
            return current_value
        try:
            pair = self.affine(chosen)[var]
        except KeyError as err:
            composed = self.affine(chosen)
            raise KeyError(
                f"No data variable named {var!r} in the composed affine view; "
                f"available: {sorted(str(key) for key in composed)}"
            ) from err
        from .binding import lift_state_if_symbolic

        pair_lifted = lift_state_if_symbolic(x, pair)
        return x * pair_lifted["scale"] + pair_lifted["center"]

    # -- state artifact ------------------------------------------------------

    def to_state_tree(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> xr.DataTree:
        """Assemble the pipeline state into a single-leaf-per-step DataTree."""
        return state_tree(state)

    # -- spec serialization ---------------------------------------------------

    def to_spec(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize into a plain-dict recipe spec, steps specs included."""
        steps = [[name, to_spec(step)] for name, step in self.steps]
        return {"kind": "Pipeline", "kwargs": {"steps": steps}}

    @classmethod
    def from_spec(cls, spec: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Pipeline:
        """Rebuild a Pipeline from a ``to_spec`` recipe."""
        steps = [
            (name, from_spec(step) if step != "passthrough" else step)
            for name, step in spec["kwargs"]["steps"]
        ]
        return cls(steps=steps)

def unscale(self, x: Any, *, var: str, state: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Any:
    """Convert a scaled-space contribution back into real units — one verb.

    For affine pipelines this applies the composed ``(center, scale)``
    pair per variable (symbolic ``pytensor.xtensor`` contributions com-
    pose identically). For pipelines that contain non-affine steps (e.g.
    a log transform on this variable) the fallback walks *this varia-
    ble's own* steps backwards — un-log, un-scale — stopping at the step
    that *created* the variable (e.g. ``Derive``), so the result is the
    pre-pipeline value of that variable in real units, not a knock-on
    restoration of unrelated inputs. `var` names a **data variable** of
    the contributions (never a coordinate). The state defaults to the
    fitted ``states_``; pass ``state=`` explicitly for pipelines rebuilt
    from specs.
    """
    chosen = state if state is not None else self.states_
    if chosen is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Pipeline has no fitted state (was this pipeline rebuilt with "
            "from_spec?); pass state=<state> explicitly or bind one"
        )
    if any(getattr(step, "affine_view", None) is None for _, step in self.steps):
        # non-affine pipeline: partial inverse — from the last step back,
        # owned variables are inverted; creation steps STOP the walk
        current_value: Any = xr.Dataset({var: x}) if isinstance(x, xr.DataArray) else x
        if var not in current_value.data_vars:
            raise KeyError(
                f"No data variable named {var!r}; variables: {sorted(map(str, current_value.data_vars))}"
            )
        for name, step in reversed(self.steps):
            step_state = chosen[name]
            if _step_creates_var(step, step_state, var):
                break  # stop *before* the step that created the variable
            if _step_owns(step, step_state, var):
                current_value = step.inverse_transform(current_value, step_state)
        if isinstance(x, xr.DataArray):
            return current_value[var]
        return current_value
    try:
        pair = self.affine(chosen)[var]
    except KeyError as err:
        composed = self.affine(chosen)
        raise KeyError(
            f"No data variable named {var!r} in the composed affine view; "
            f"available: {sorted(str(key) for key in composed)}"
        ) from err
    from .binding import lift_state_if_symbolic

    pair_lifted = lift_state_if_symbolic(x, pair)
    return x * pair_lifted["scale"] + pair_lifted["center"]

items.text:
Many pipelines over the same dataset, merged back into one container.

sklearn's FeatureUnion/make_union composition, xarray-native: every branch fits and transforms the input independently; the outputs are merged by variable name under a collision policy.

  • collisions="require_equal" (default): variables present in several branches must transform identically — shared passthroughs merge silently, genuinely conflicting recipes raise naming branch+variable.
  • collisions="error": branches must produce disjoint variable sets.
  • collisions="keep_first": first branch wins; discouraged (silent).

The state nests one level per branch ({"branch": branch_state}), so state_tree makes the whole fitted union a single artifact. inverse_transform runs each branch's chain backwards, then applies the same collision policy — derived variables get dropped per-branch, so pipelines containing unions still round-trip.

Unions are non-affine by design: Pipeline.affine() refuses pipelines containing one (the covariates-only pattern; real-terms conversion for target-like paths goes through inverse_transform).

class Union:
    """Many pipelines over the same dataset, merged back into one container.

    sklearn's ``FeatureUnion``/``make_union`` composition, xarray-native:
    every branch fits and transforms the input independently; the outputs are
    merged by variable name under a collision policy.

    - ``collisions="require_equal"`` (default): variables present in several
      branches must transform identically — shared passthroughs merge
      silently, genuinely conflicting recipes raise naming branch+variable.
    - ``collisions="error"``: branches must produce disjoint variable sets.
    - ``collisions="keep_first"``: first branch wins; discouraged (silent).

    The state nests one level per branch (``{"branch": branch_state}``), so
    ``state_tree`` makes the whole fitted union a single artifact.
    ``inverse_transform`` runs each branch's chain backwards, then applies the
    same collision policy — derived variables get dropped per-branch, so
    pipelines containing unions still round-trip.

    Unions are **non-affine by design**: ``Pipeline.affine()`` refuses
    pipelines containing one (the covariates-only pattern; real-terms
    conversion for target-like paths goes through ``inverse_transform``).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        branches: list[tuple[str, Any]],
        collisions: str = "require_equal",
    ):
        """Take named ``(name, branch)`` pairs and the collision policy."""
        if collisions not in {"require_equal", "error", "keep_first"}:
            raise ValueError(f"collisions must be require_equal | error | keep_first; got {collisions!r}")
        # de-duplicate branch names the same way make_pipeline does
        seen: dict[str, int] = {}
        resolved: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
        for name, transformer in branches:
            count = seen.get(name, 0) + 1
            seen[name] = count
            resolved.append((name if count == 1 else f"{name}-{count - 1}", transformer))
        self.branches = resolved
        self.collisions = collisions
        self.states_: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    # -- sklearn-composite API -----------------------------------------------

    def fit(self, X: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Fit every branch against the same input ``X``."""
        states: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, branch in self.branches:
            states[name] = branch.fit(X)
        self.states_ = states
        return states

    def transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Transform ``X`` through every branch and merge the outputs."""
        merged: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, branch in self.branches:
            out = branch.transform(X, state[name])
            self._merge(merged, _flatten(out), name)
        return _reassemble(X, merged)

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
        """Invert every branch on ``X`` and merge, dropping lost variables.

        A variable dropped by any branch is dropped from the result (each
        branch removes its own derived vars); variables surviving in every
        branch must restore identically.
        """
        dropped: set[str] = set()
        outputs: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
        for name, branch in reversed(self.branches):
            flat = _flatten(branch.inverse_transform(X, state[name]))
            dropped |= {key for key in _flatten(X) if key not in flat}
            outputs.append(flat)
        out = {key: value for key, value in outputs[0].items() if key not in dropped}
        return _reassemble(X, out)

    def fit_transform(self, X: Any) -> Any:
        """Fit on ``X`` and return the merged transformed data."""
        state = self.fit(X)
        return self.transform(X, state)

    def _merge(
        self,
        merged: dict[str, Any],
        branch_out: Mapping[str, Any],
        branch: str,
    ) -> None:
        for key, value in branch_out.items():
            if key not in merged:
                merged[key] = value
                continue
            existing = merged[key]
            if self.collisions == "keep_first":
                continue
            if isinstance(existing, xr.DataArray) and isinstance(value, xr.DataArray):
                same_dims = existing.dims == value.dims
                same_values = same_dims and bool(np.allclose(existing.values, value.values, equal_nan=True))
                if same_values:
                    continue
            if self.collisions == "require_equal":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Union branches {branch!r} and an earlier branch produce conflicting "
                    f"values for variable {key!r} (collisions={self.collisions!r}); "
                    "either scale a variable in one branch only, or pass collisions='error'/'keep_first'"
                )
            raise ValueError(
                f"Union: variable {key!r} collides between branches under collisions={self.collisions!r}"
            )

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> BoundStep:
        """Access one fitted branch: ``union["name"]`` as a BoundStep."""
        if self.states_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Union is not fitted; call fit() before step access")
        steps = dict(self.branches)
        if key not in steps:
            raise KeyError(f"No branch named {key!r}. Branches: {sorted(steps)}")
        return BoundStep(key, steps[key], self.states_[key])

    # -- affine / real-units conversion --------------------------------------

    def affine(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, xr.Dataset]:
        """Composed (center, scale) per variable, resolved across branches.

        A variable owned by exactly one affine branch gets that branch's
        composed pair. A variable appearing under several branches is
        arbitrated by ``self.collisions`` exactly as in ``transform``:
        values must agree (or ``keep_first`` wins); genuinely conflicting
        pairs raise naming the branches. A branch that is not affine makes
        the whole call raise, naming the branch — runs the same
        "refuse rather than return a wrong pair" policy as
        ``Pipeline.affine``, per variable rather than per structure.
        """
        composed: dict[str, xr.Dataset] = {}
        owners: dict[str, str] = {}
        for (name, branch), branch_state in zip(self.branches, state.values(), strict=True):
            # a branch is either a leaf scaler (affine_view) or a composite
            # (Pipeline/Union with its own affine()) — resolve either
            view = getattr(branch, "affine_view", None)
            if view is not None:
                branch_pairs = view(branch_state)
            elif hasattr(branch, "affine"):
                branch_pairs = branch.affine(branch_state)
            else:
                raise TypeError(
                    f"Union branch {name!r} ({type(branch).__name__}) is not "
                    "affine; the composed affine view is undefined"
                )
            for key, pair in branch_pairs.items():
                if key in composed:
                    prev = composed[key]
                    same = self.collisions == "keep_first" or (
                        pair["center"].identical(prev["center"]) and pair["scale"].identical(prev["scale"])
                    )
                    if not same:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Union branches {owners[key]!r} and {name!r} produce "
                            f"conflicting affine pairs for variable {key!r} "
                            f"(collisions={self.collisions!r})"
                        )
                    continue
                composed[key] = xr.Dataset({"center": pair["center"], "scale": pair["scale"]})
                owners[key] = name
        return composed

    def unscale(self, x: Any, *, var: str, state: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> Any:
        """Convert a scaled-space value of ``var`` back into real units.

        Same verb, same semantics as ``Pipeline.unscale``: the composed
        affine pair from ``affine`` for variables owned by affine
        branches. Variables whose owning branch is not affine raise, naming
        the workaround (per-branch inverse) rather than guessing.
        """
        chosen = state if state is not None else self.states_
        if chosen is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Union has no fitted state; pass state=<state> or bind one")
        try:
            pair = self.affine(chosen)[var]
        except KeyError as err:
            raise KeyError(
                f"No data variable named {var!r} in the union's affine view; "
                "branches must contain affine scalers for this variable"
            ) from err
        from .binding import lift_state_if_symbolic

        pair_lifted = lift_state_if_symbolic(x, pair)
        return x * pair_lifted["scale"] + pair_lifted["center"]

    # -- spec serialization ----------------------------------------------------

    def to_spec(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize into a plain-dict recipe spec, branch specs included."""
        return {
            "kind": "Union",
            "kwargs": {
                "branches": [[name, to_spec(branch)] for name, branch in self.branches],
                "collisions": self.collisions,
            },
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_spec(cls, spec: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Union:
        """Rebuild a Union from a ``to_spec`` recipe."""
        branches = [
            (name, from_spec(spec_branch) if spec_branch != "passthrough" else spec_branch)
            for name, spec_branch in spec["kwargs"]["branches"]
        ]
        return cls(branches=branches, collisions=spec["kwargs"]["collisions"])

Transformers, mirroring sklearn.preprocessing.

Two families live here, both of which sklearn also keeps in sklearn.preprocessing:

  • the scalers — ZScore, MeanScaler, FixedScaler (all affine, y = (x - center) / scale) and Func for named elementwise ops (log, log1p, ... — the FunctionTransformer analog);
  • the steps that build, split or select variables rather than rescaling them — Derive (a new variable from selected pieces, the PolynomialFeatures analog), Splitter and Selector.

Everything affine exposes state keys center and scale (z-score's mean/std map onto this pair, matching PR-2831).

items.title: Derive
items.text:
Derive a new variable from selected pieces of existing variables.

Pieces reference (var_name, sel), so the two sides need not come from the same variable or the same grain — xarray broadcasting does the rest. A national series over a product-grain control, giving a product-grain derived variable:

Derive(
    name="tv_per_control",
    left=("media_national", {"media": "tv"}),
    right=("controls_prod", {}),
    op="ratio",
)

The within-one-variable shape works the same way, selecting coordinate values out of a variable that carries an extra coordinate dimension:

Derive(
    name="level_ratio",
    left=("controls", {"control": "level"}),
    right=("controls", {"control": "reference"}),
    op="ratio",
)
  • selectors are the same Splitter-style label dict, so lists + reduce (sum | mean | first | last) cover share-of-total style derivations, while scalar selections pass through directly.
  • ops: ratio | diff | product — a closed named vocabulary, because specs must stay plain JSON (no lambdas).

@register
class Derive:
    """Derive a new variable from selected pieces of existing variables.

    Pieces reference ``(var_name, sel)``, so the two sides need not come from
    the same variable or the same grain — xarray broadcasting does the rest.
    A national series over a product-grain control, giving a product-grain
    derived variable:

        Derive(
            name="tv_per_control",
            left=("media_national", {"media": "tv"}),
            right=("controls_prod", {}),
            op="ratio",
        )

    The within-one-variable shape works the same way, selecting coordinate
    values out of a variable that carries an extra coordinate dimension:

        Derive(
            name="level_ratio",
            left=("controls", {"control": "level"}),
            right=("controls", {"control": "reference"}),
            op="ratio",
        )

    - selectors are the same ``Splitter``-style label dict, so lists +
      ``reduce`` (sum | mean | first | last) cover share-of-total style
      derivations, while scalar selections pass through directly.
    - ops: ``ratio`` | ``diff`` | ``product`` — a closed named vocabulary,
      because specs must stay plain JSON (no lambdas).
    - stateless: ``fit`` records only the recipe; ``inverse_transform``
      drops the derived variable (its inputs survive untouched), so a
      pipeline containing it still round-trips.
    - Dataset inputs only (DataTree derivation is deferred; the derived var
      needs a flat variable namespace).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        left: tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
        right: tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
        *,
        op: str = "ratio",
        reduce: str | None = None,
    ):
        """``left op right`` — neutral names over the closed op vocabulary."""
        if op not in {"ratio", "diff", "product"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Derive ops are ratio | diff | product; got {op!r}")
        if right is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Derive op={op!r} needs a right piece")
        if reduce is not None and reduce not in {"sum", "mean", "first", "last"}:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported reduce {reduce!r}; use sum | mean | first | last")
        self.name: str = name
        self.left = self._normalize_piece(left)
        self.right = self._normalize_piece(right)
        self.op = op
        self.reduce = reduce

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_piece(piece: Any) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Accept ``(var, sel)`` tuples or serialized ``{"var", "sel"}`` dicts."""
        if isinstance(piece, dict):
            return str(piece["var"]), dict(piece["sel"])
        return str(piece[0]), dict(piece[1])

    def to_spec_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize the derive recipe into JSON-safe kwargs."""
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "left": {"var": self.left[0], "sel": self._jsonable_sel(self.left[1])},
            "right": None
            if self.right is None
            else {"var": self.right[0], "sel": self._jsonable_sel(self.right[1])},
            "op": self.op,
            "reduce": self.reduce,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _jsonable_sel(sel: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {dim: list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) else value for dim, value in sel.items()}

    def to_spec(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize the derive recipe."""
        from .serialize import spec_of

        return spec_of(self)

    # -- pieces --------------------------------------------------------------

    def _piece(self, X: xr.Dataset, piece: tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None) -> xr.DataArray:
        var, sel = piece if piece is not None else (None, {})
        da = X[var]
        sel_args: dict[str, Any] = {
            str(dim): list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) else value for dim, value in sel.items()
        }
        for dim, value in sel_args.items():
            da = da.sel(**{dim: value})
        reduce = self.reduce
        needs_reduce = any(isinstance(v, (list, tuple)) and len(v) > 1 for v in sel.values())
        if reduce and needs_reduce:
            da = getattr(da, reduce)(dim=list(sel))
        elif reduce is not None and needs_reduce:
            raise ValueError(f"reduce={reduce!r} is not a recognized reducer")
        return da

    # -- transformer API -------------------------------------------------------

    def fit(self, X: Any) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Validate pieces exist, then record the derived name and op."""
        if not isinstance(X, xr.Dataset):
            raise TypeError("Derive works on Dataset inputs (DataTree derivation deferred)")
        for piece in (self.left, self.right):
            if piece is None:
                continue
            var = piece[0]
            if var not in X.data_vars:
                raise KeyError(f"Derive piece references unknown variable {var!r}")
        derived = self.name
        if X is not None and derived in X.data_vars:
            raise ValueError(f"Derived variable name {derived!r} already exists")
        return _stamp_state(
            as_state(
                "derive",
                None,
                scaled_from=None,
                attrs={
                    "derived": self.name,
                    "op": self.op,
                    "reduce": self.reduce or "",
                },
            ),
            self,
        )

    @classmethod
    def describe(cls, spec):
        """One created row for the derived variable, affine by op."""
        from .serialize import _recipe_line

        return [
            {
                "variable": spec["name"],
                "role": "created",
                "kind": "Derive",
                "recipe": _recipe_line({"kind": "Derive", "kwargs": spec}),
                "op": str(spec.get("op", "") or ""),
                "affine": True,
            }
        ]

    def transform(self, X: Any, state: xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Select the two pieces, apply the op, and append the new variable."""
        if not isinstance(X, xr.Dataset):
            raise TypeError("Derive works on Dataset inputs")
        first = self._piece(X, self.left)
        second = self._piece(X, self.right)
        if self.op == "ratio":
            derived = first / second
        elif self.op == "diff":
            derived = first - second
        else:
            derived = first * second
        out = {key: da for key, da in flatten(X).items()}
        out[self.name] = derived.rename(self.name)
        return reassemble(X, out)

    def inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Drop the derived variable, restoring the original variables."""
        out = {key: da for key, da in flatten(X).items() if key != state.attrs["derived"]}
        return reassemble(X, out)

@register
class EwmSmooth(BaseTransformer):
    """Causal exponential smoothing: ``s_t = a*x_t + (1-a)*s_{t-1}``.

    Seeds at the first value (``s_0 = x_0``), so smoothing a fresh block of
    data burns in from that block's own values and never yields NaN, mirroring
    ``RollingMean``. Out-of-sample: ``transform`` needs only the fitted
    ``alpha`` (state) and the X it is handed; for boundary continuity concat
    the in-sample tail with the new block and slice afterwards.

    One named dim to smooth over: ``dims=("date",)`` or equivalent; an
    ambiguous ``dims=None`` on multi-dim data raises. Internal NaNs in X
    propagate through the recursion (a missing value never recovers).

    Not affine: ``Pipeline.affine()`` refuses pipelines containing it, and
    ``inverse_transform`` honestly raises. xarray-only: no symbolic
    (``pytensor.xtensor``) path.
    """

    def __init__(self, alpha: float = 0.5, dims: tuple[str, ...] | str | None = None):
        """Take the recursion weight ``alpha`` in ``(0, 1]`` and the dim."""
        if not 0 < alpha <= 1:
            raise ValueError(f"alpha must be in (0, 1]; got {alpha}")
        super().__init__(dims)
        self.alpha = alpha

    def to_spec_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize alpha and dims into plain-dict kwargs."""
        return {"alpha": self.alpha, "dims": self.dims}

    def compute(self, X: Any) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Record the recursion weight (the only fitted knowledge)."""
        if is_symbolic(X):
            raise NotImplementedError("EwmSmooth is xarray-only (no symbolic path)")
        self._smooth_dim(X)
        scaled_from = getattr(X, "name", None)
        return as_state("ewm", self.dims, scaled_from, attrs={"alpha": self.alpha})

    def _smooth_dim(self, X: Any) -> str:
        """Resolve the single dim the recursion runs along."""
        dims = self._reduce_dims(X)
        if len(dims) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"EwmSmooth smooths exactly one dim; resolved {dims}. Pass dims=<dim name> explicitly."
            )
        return dims[0]

    def _transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        if is_symbolic(X):
            raise NotImplementedError("EwmSmooth is xarray-only (no symbolic path)")
        alpha = float(getattr(state, "attrs", {}).get("alpha", self.alpha))
        axis = X.get_axis_num(self._smooth_dim(X))
        values = np.moveaxis(np.asarray(X, dtype=float), axis, 0)
        decay = 1.0 - alpha
        out = np.empty(values.shape, dtype=float)
        out[0] = values[0]
        prev = out[0]
        for t in range(1, values.shape[0]):
            prev = alpha * values[t] + decay * prev
            out[t] = prev
        out = np.moveaxis(out, 0, axis)
        return xr.DataArray(out, coords=X.coords, dims=X.dims).assign_attrs(X.attrs)

    def _inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Mapping[str, xr.DataArray] | xr.Dataset) -> Any:
        """Smoothing mixes history; raising is the contract, not a guess."""
        raise NonInvertibleError(
            "EwmSmooth recursively mixes history; inverse_transform cannot "
            "honestly restore the original series (the seed is lost)."
        )

@register
class FunctionTransformer(BaseTransformer):
    """Named elementwise transform per variable — non-affine on purpose.

    The second half of the "ratio, then log" chain: after a ``Derive`` step
    produces a derived metric, apply a named unary function (e.g. ``log``) to
    selected variables. Unmapped variables pass through unchanged.

    Because it is not affine, ``Pipeline.affine()`` refuses pipelines that
    contain it (by design): if the *target* is log-transformed, real-terms
    contributions must go through ``inverse_transform`` — the batched path —
    rather than the ``β·scale`` shortcut.
    """

    def __init__(self, mapping: dict[str, str]):
        """Take ``{variable: op}`` pairs; ops are named unary functions."""
        unknown = {op for op in mapping.values() if op not in _FUNC_INVERSES}
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown functions {sorted(unknown)}; known: {sorted(_FUNC_INVERSES)}")
        self.mapping = dict(mapping)

    def to_spec_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize the variable-to-op mapping into plain-dict kwargs."""
        return {"mapping": dict(self.mapping)}

    @classmethod
    def describe(cls, spec):
        """One non-affine transformed row per mapped variable."""
        from .serialize import _recipe_line

        recipe = _recipe_line({"kind": "FunctionTransformer", "kwargs": spec})
        return [
            {
                "variable": variable,
                "role": "transformed",
                "kind": "FunctionTransformer",
                "recipe": recipe,
                "op": str(op),
                "affine": False,
            }
            for variable, op in spec["mapping"].items()
        ]

    def compute(self, X: Any) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Record which named function applies per variable (netCDF-safe)."""
        name = getattr(X, "name", None)
        scaled_from = str(name) if name is not None else ""
        # the mapping lives on the *recipe*; each per-variable state carries
        # only the scalar op decision for that variable (netCDF-safe)
        return as_state(
            "function",
            None,
            scaled_from,
            attrs={
                # None → "" for netCDF-safety (scalar string attrs only)
                "op": self.mapping.get(scaled_from, ""),
            },
        )

    def _transform(self, X: Any, state: Any) -> Any:
        op = state.attrs.get("op", "")
        if not op:
            return X
        return getattr(np, op)(X)

    def _inverse_transform(self, X: Any, state: Any) -> Any:
        op = state.attrs.get("op", "")
        if not op:
            return X
        return getattr(np, _FUNC_INVERSES[op])(X)
